Petrovirivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Petrovirivka, Ukraine

Not demolished. Established no later than 1840 per its oldest gravestone, this cemetery appears on a 1941 Russian military map, and postwar gravestones confirm continued Jewish presence after the war. Jewish settlement began in the late 19th century; population reached 819 by 1897 and 1,557 (97%) by 1926. A 1920s-30s elementary school and rural council served the community, with Jews organized into artisan cooperatives; three nearby agricultural colonies formed - Frayland (38 families), Ratenfeld (60 families), and Rayzenfeld (59 families, 258 people). Population fell to 470 by 1939. Nazi occupation from August 7, 1941 murdered about 75 Jews by September; over 200 Jews in total fell victim to the Nazi regime.
